```gherkin
@version-endpoint
Feature: Version Endpoint
  As an operator of the api_test service
  I want to read the version metadata of the running service
  So that I can confirm exactly which build is serving traffic

  Background:
    Given the api_test service is running

  # Why: Core read path — the minimal complete definition of the feature
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Reading the version metadata returns the complete set of fields
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then the request should succeed
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The application version string is available at runtime from application or build metadata
    And the response should include the application version
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The git commit hash of the running build is injected at build time and readable at runtime
    And the response should include the git commit the running build was made from
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The service name is sourced from the service's existing runtime configuration
    And the response should include the service name

  # Why: The endpoint is public, matching the access pattern of the existing uptime and stats endpoints
  @key-example
  Scenario: Version metadata is readable without authentication
    Given I am not authenticated
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then the request should succeed
    And the version metadata should be complete

  # Why: At-the-limit boundary — the documented shape is exactly three fields, no more and no fewer
  @boundary
  Scenario: The version response contains exactly the three documented fields
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then the response should contain exactly three fields
    And those fields should be the application version, the git commit, and the service name

  # Why: Minimum-content boundary — every field must carry a real value, never an empty one
  @boundary
  Scenario: Every version field is populated with a non-empty value
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then none of the returned fields should be empty

  # Why: Just-outside boundary of the allowed-operation set — reading is the only permitted operation
  @negative @boundary
  Scenario Outline: Write requests to the version endpoint are rejected as not allowed
    When I send a <method> request to the version endpoint
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The rejection follows the service's existing error handling conventions for disallowed methods
    Then the request should be rejected because the method is not allowed
    And the version metadata should remain unchanged

    Examples:
      | method |
      | POST   |
      | PUT    |
      | PATCH  |
      | DELETE |

  # Why: Proves the documented no-database constraint — version metadata must not depend on any data store
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Version metadata stays available when the data store is unavailable
    Given the service's data store is unavailable
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then the request should succeed
    And the version metadata should be complete

  # Why: Read-only stability — repeated reads of the same running build never disagree
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Repeated reads return identical version metadata
    Given I have already read the version metadata
    When I read the version metadata again
    Then both responses should be identical

  # Why: The metadata must describe the build actually serving traffic, not a stale one
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Version metadata identifies the newly deployed build after a redeploy
    Given a new build of the service has been deployed
    When I request the service's version metadata
    Then the git commit should identify the newly deployed build
```

```markdown
**Stack**: generic

## Scope

The api_test service gains a read-only /version endpoint returning exactly three JSON fields — the application version string, the git commit the running build was made from, and the service name — with all three fields guaranteed non-empty. The specification covers the successful unauthenticated read path, the exact three-field response shape, rejection of all write methods (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) as not allowed, and independence from any database, mirroring the existing /uptime and /stats endpoints.
```
